# restate_kafka_cluster (Resource)

A Kafka cluster connection configuration, which `restate_subscription` references by name.

`properties` are librdkafka configuration properties and can contain SASL passwords and TLS key material, so the whole map is sensitive and is stored in Terraform state. **Use an encrypted, access-controlled state backend.**

The Admin API redacts sensitive property values when it reads a cluster back, so the provider keeps the configured value for any property it cannot verify -- either because the API visibly redacted it, or because the property's name marks its value as secret. Non-secret properties are still compared against the API, so a genuine out-of-band change is reported as drift.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Properties can contain SASL passwords and TLS key material, so the whole map is sensitive and is
# stored in Terraform state. Use an encrypted, access-controlled state backend.
#
# The Admin API redacts sensitive values when it reads a cluster back, so the provider keeps the
# configured value for anything it cannot verify. Non-secret properties are still compared against
# the API, so a genuine out-of-band change shows as drift.

resource "restate_kafka_cluster" "events" {
  name = "events"

  properties = {
    "bootstrap.servers" = "broker-1.kafka.example.com:9092,broker-2.kafka.example.com:9092"
    "security.protocol" = "SASL_SSL"
    "sasl.mechanism"    = "SCRAM-SHA-512"
    "sasl.username"     = "restate"
    "sasl.password"     = var.kafka_password
  }

  # Leave this false so the API's own dependency check stays in charge: deleting a cluster that
  # subscriptions still reference would orphan them. Delete the subscriptions instead.
  force_destroy = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Cluster name, used by subscriptions to reference this cluster. Must be a valid hostname.

Changing it **replaces** the cluster: the Admin API addresses updates by name, so a rename is a different cluster. Any subscription referencing the old name must be updated too.
- `properties` (Map of String, Sensitive) librdkafka configuration properties. Must set one of `bootstrap.servers` or `metadata.broker.list` to identify the brokers; the provider checks this before sending the request.

See the [librdkafka configuration reference](https://github.com/confluentinc/librdkafka/blob/master/CONFIGURATION.md) for the full list. The whole map is sensitive and is redacted from provider logs and diagnostics.

An update replaces the entire map, so a property omitted from a later apply is removed from the cluster.

### Optional

- `force_destroy` (Boolean) Delete the cluster even when subscriptions still reference it, **orphaning those subscriptions**.

By default the provider does not send the API's `force` parameter, leaving the server's own dependency check in charge: a delete with attached subscriptions is refused, and the error says so. Prefer deleting the subscriptions instead.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the cluster configuration was created.
- `id` (String) Same as `name`. The Admin API addresses a cluster by name, so the name is the identity; this exists because Terraform tooling expects an `id`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Clusters are addressed by name, which is their identity.
#
# Sensitive property values come back redacted and an import has no configured values to fall back
# on, so state holds the API's placeholders rather than real credentials. Put the real values in your
# configuration and apply before relying on the cluster; the provider warns about this on import.
terraform import restate_kafka_cluster.events events
```
